question: US x Iran diplomatic meeting by July 31, 2026?
resolution_criteria:
On June 22, the first round of U.S.-Iran diplomatic talks in Switzerland concluded, with mediators reporting progress toward a roadmap for a final deal and follow-on technical talks expected to continue.(see: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/6/22/us-iran-agree-on-roadmap-towards-final-deal-in-switzerland-talks). 

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the next formal senior-level round of peace talks between representatives of the United States and Iran begins by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

A qualifying round must be a deliberate in-person diplomatic meeting or negotiating round concerning US-Iran relations, involving senior representatives of both the United States and Iran who are acting in an official capacity and are authorized to conduct or materially direct diplomacy on behalf of their governments.

Indirect in-person diplomacy through designated mediators, facilitators, or interlocutors will qualify, provided senior representatives of both the United States and Iran are participating in the same formal diplomatic process with the knowledge and authorization of their respective governments. The representatives need not be in the same room at the same time.

Follow-on technical talks from the June 22 Switzerland round will not qualify by themselves. Technical, staff-level, working-group, implementation, monitoring, preparatory, or deconfliction meetings will not qualify unless they occur as part of a new formally convened senior-level U.S.-Iran peace-talks round.

Brief greetings, chance encounters, photo opportunities, ceremonial appearances, or talks not deliberately aimed at diplomacy or negotiation will not count.

The meeting must be in-person (including indirect in-person meetings) and must be publicly acknowledged by either government or reported by a consensus of credible media. Remote meetings, phone calls, or other meetings where the relevant parties are not present will not count.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran, and a consensus of credible reporting.

I'm writing up the findings now. Several page fetches were blocked, so most of the facts below come from search-result summaries.

# US x Iran senior-level meeting by July 31, 2026: research as of 2026-07-11

## 1. Resolution source
- I could not open the Al Jazeera article named in the criteria because the proxy refused the connection. Other outlets describe the same round:
- 2026-06-21/22: US Vice President JD Vance and Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf led delegations at Bürgenstock, Switzerland. Pakistan and Qatar mediated. They agreed a "roadmap towards reaching a final deal within 60 days" and a contact channel to keep the Strait of Hormuz open. [Bloomberg Law](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/bloomberg-government-news/us-iran-begin-talks-in-switzerland-on-permanent-peace-deal-2)
- 2026-06-22: Switzerland said the roadmap "creates the conditions for the immediate resumption of new technical discussions." Under the market rules, those technical talks do not count. [Arab News PK](https://www.arabnews.pk/node/2648113), [APP](https://www.app.com.pk/?p=1231060)
- The question resolves on US and Iranian government statements and a consensus of credible media. There is no single data series.

## 2. Current status
- As of 2026-07-11 I found no confirmed senior-level round after June 22. Nothing settles the question yet.
- The background has turned hostile. US strikes resumed in early July, and Trump declared the interim memorandum (the "Islamabad MoU") "over" on July 8, while saying talks might continue.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-07-10: Al Jazeera says the US struck Iran that week, the third time it has done so while talks were ongoing. A US official said technical talks would continue; Trump said the MoU was "over." [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/10/us-iran-war-will-peace-talks-ever-resume-and-when)
- 2026-07-10: Headline: "Trump hints at further Iran negotiations after exchange of fire over Hormuz." I could not fetch the article. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/10/trump-says-us-has-agreed-to-continue-iran-talks-but-ceasefire-over)
- 2026-07-08: Trump said the interim deal was over after Iranian attacks on tankers near Hormuz. He reimposed a naval blockade of Iranian ports, revoked an oil sanctions waiver, and US forces hit about 90 Iranian military targets. He said he "might" let talks continue but called them a "waste of time." Iranian Deputy FM Gharibabadi said Tehran had suspended its own commitments under the MoU (exact date of his remark unclear). [ABC News](https://abcnews.com/International/trump-mou-calls-iranian-leaders-scum-latest-strikes/story?id=134576539), [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/8/why-have-us-iran-strikes-resumed-and-what-does-it-mean-for-peace-talks), [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/07/08/world/live-news/iran-war-nato-summit-ukraine-trump)
- 2026-07-08: Wikipedia lists the Islamabad MoU as expiring on 8 July 2026. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamabad_Memorandum)
- 2026-07-04: Report that the next US-Iran talks were set for Pakistan on July 11, with Bürgenstock as a backup venue. Search summaries call this a "technical" round, so it may not qualify. Strikes since then have probably derailed it, though I could not confirm that. [Newsmax](https://www.newsmax.com/newsfront/us-iran-talks/2026/07/04/id/1261765/), [Deccan Herald](https://www.deccanherald.com/world/pakistan/next-round-of-us-iran-talks-likely-to-be-held-in-islamabad-report-4062765)
- 2026-07-01: Qatar said indirect meetings in Doha were making "positive progress." Vance said talks were "going well." The next meeting was to be set after the funeral processions for Ali Khamenei. [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/07/01/world/live-news/iran-war-trump)

## 4. Base rates
- Senior-level rounds in 2026 that I could identify:
  - April: Vance and Ghalibaf in Islamabad, a two-day round.
  - Around April 22: a planned second Islamabad round collapsed. Trump cancelled the US envoys' trip, and Iran refused direct talks. [AA](https://aa.com.tr/en/world/us-vice-president-extends-stay-in-islamabad-at-pakistans-request-as-us-iran-talks-stretch-into-2nd-day-sources/3902496), [NBC](https://www.nbcnews.com/world/iran/live-blog/live-updates-us-envoys-heading-pakistan-uncertainty-iran-talks-rcna342031), [CBS](https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/us-iran-war-trump-strait-of-hormuz-hezbollah-lebanon-israel-ceasefire/)
  - June 21-22: Bürgenstock.
- That is roughly one formal senior-level round every 1 to 2 months. Announced rounds have often slipped or been cancelled, especially after military escalation.
- It is unclear whether the July 1 Doha meetings were senior-level.
- 2025 comparison: Witkoff and Araghchi held about five Oman-mediated rounds from April to June 2025, roughly one every 1 to 3 weeks, until the June 2025 strikes halted them.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket runs this market, "Next round of US-Iran peace talks by...?" (event created 2026-06-23). The page would not load, so I could not get current prices. A search summary said traders had low confidence in talks by mid-to-late July, but I could not verify that. [Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/next-round-of-us-iran-peace-talks-byptptpt-20260623022722982)
- I found no Kalshi or Manifold prices, and no expert forecasts.

## 6. Upcoming events before July 31
- Whether the reported July 11 Islamabad or Bürgenstock meeting happens, and at what level. A technical-only meeting would not count.
- Trump's decision on whether to allow talks to continue, and whether strikes and the blockade go on.
- Iran's stance after suspending its MoU commitments, and any timing effects from the Khamenei funeral and mourning period.
- Mediation by Pakistan, Qatar and Switzerland. The 60-day roadmap window from June 22 runs to about August 21.
- Any new ceasefire, which could quickly lead to a senior-level round.

Sources: the links given inline above.
